samples.evidence: The diff changes four production sites in text-editor.ts that stamp affinity onto a selection endpoint: mousedown (`pos` now carries `result.lineAffinity`, ~line 1517), the HF drag and body drag handlers (~1773/1795), the shift+arrow focus (`focus: { ...newPos, lineAffinity: focusAffinity }`, ~2775) and shift+Home (`lineAffinity: 'forward'`, ~2808). The only new test, packages/docs/test/view/selection-line-affinity.test.ts, calls `computeSelectionRects` directly with hand-authored endpoint objects that already contain `lineAffinity`; it never constructs a TextEditor and never dispatches a mouse or key event. Grepping packages/docs/test for `handleMouseDown|getPositionFromMouse|mousedown` returns no files, and `lineAffinity` appears in only one other docs test (hf-caret-selection.test.ts, which covers `computeHFCursorPixel`, not selection endpoints). So if any of these producer sites dropped or set the wrong affinity, every test in the repo would still pass — the suite proves only that the consumer honours a field, not that anyone ever sets it. The repo does support driving this (backward-selection-toggle.test.ts uses `dispatchKey(container, ..., { shiftKey: true })`), so the gap is not a tooling limitation.

verdict.reason: The five text-editor producer sites that stamp lineAffinity onto selection endpoints (text-editor.ts:1517-1525 mousedown, :1773-1779 HF drag, :1795-1799 body drag, :2772-2780 shift+arrow focus, :2811-2814 shift+Home focus) have no test anywhere in the repo. No docs test dispatches mousedown/pointerdown (only a contextmenu event in editor-contextmenu.test.ts:68-77), and the sole shift+arrow test (editor-read-only.test.ts:341-362) asserts only anchor/focus offsets and unchanged text, passing regardless of affinity. Frontend docs tests dispatch no KeyboardEvent/MouseEvent at all. So all five affinity-producing branches could drop or invert the value with the suite still green: a clear behavior change with no meaningful test, major under the missing-tests rule.

Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a changed behavior shipped with no meaningful test covering it — major.

finding.summary: None of the text-editor plumbing that actually produces the affinity is tested (click, shift+click, drag, shift+Home, shift+arrow)
finding.evidence: The user-visible fix is that a click/drag/caret-move on a wrap boundary tags the selection endpoint with `lineAffinity` (text-editor.ts ~1517 mousedown, ~1770 header/footer drag, ~1792 body drag, ~2772 shift+arrow, ~2805 shift+Home). The only new test, packages/docs/test/view/selection-line-affinity.test.ts, hand-constructs DocPositions and calls `computeSelectionRects` directly — it never goes through TextEditor, so it cannot fail if the editor forgets to attach the affinity, attaches the wrong one (e.g. the shift+Home hardcoded 'forward' at offset 0, or shift+Up/Down using the cursor's stale affinity), or drops it on `setRange`. I grepped packages/docs/test for `lineAffinity` (only the new file and hf-caret-selection.test.ts, which tests computeHFCursorPixel), and for `Home|getVisualLineStart|updateDragSelection|mousedown|mousemove` (only cursor-move-no-relayout.test.ts and image-selection-overlay.test.ts, neither of which touches selection affinity). Result: the entire producer side ships with zero coverage while the rect consumer is well covered.

verdict.reason:
The claim holds up. text-editor.ts really does contain the new producer plumbing the reviewer describes: mousedown builds a DocPosition with `lineAffinity` from the hit and feeds it to `setRange`/`cursor.moveTo` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1517-1526, 1621-1626), the header/footer drag and body drag attach `result.lineAffinity` to the focus (1771-1779, 1795-1798, 1897-1904), shift+arrow picks `isVertical ? this.cursor.lineAffinity : hAffinity` for the focus (2772-2780), and shift+Home hardcodes `lineAffinity: 'forward'` on the focus (2811-2814).

Searching for a test that exercises any of those paths turned up nothing. Repo-wide, only three test files mention affinity at all: packages/docs/test/view/selection-line-affinity.test.ts (hand-builds a two-line layout and calls `computeSelectionRects` directly — I read it in full; it never constructs a TextEditor/EditorAPI, so it exercises only the consumer in selection.ts), packages/docs/test/view/hf-caret-selection.test.ts (calls `computeHFCursorPixel`/`computeHFSelectionRects` with an affinity argument passed by hand — again no editor, no mouse/key event), and packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store-concurrent.integration.ts (store-level anchor/resolve round-trip via `updateCursorPos`, and its selection-endpoint tests at :474 and :501 don't set or assert any affinity).

I also went wider than the reviewer: grepped `/ffinity/` across every `*test*|*spec*|*e2e*` file in the repo (only the two docs files), grepped the whole docs test dir for `shiftKey|dispatchEvent|mousedown|keydown` (19 files, none mention affinity — I read backward-selection-toggle.test.ts and cursor-move-no-relayout.test.ts, which drive the real editor via `_setSelectionForTest`/dispatched keydowns but only for style toggles and measure counts), grepped for `'Home'|Arrow*` in all test files, for `paginatedPixelToPosition|findPositionAtPixel|getVisualLineStart|_getCursorForTest|handleMouse` in packages/docs/test (pagination.test.ts calls `paginatedPixelToPosition` but never asserts the returned `lineAffinity`), for "wrap boundary" repo-wide, and checked for any playwright/cypress/e2e suite (none exists). The task doc docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md step 5 itself names the single rect-level test as the whole test plan while step 3 is the text-editor change.

So the consumer side is covered while every producer path (click, shift+click, body drag, header/footer drag, shift+arrow, shift+Home including its hardcoded 'forward') ships with no test that could fail if the affinity were omitted, inverted, or dropped on setRange. Under the test-adequacy rubric that is a clear behavior change with no meaningful test — major. I found no counterexample.
